notes: Requires JSON5 parser (comments not valid JSON). Covers the plugin-wide minimum (skill-authoring standard check #10, >=3 scenarios) plus every behavior added/changed in the 2026-07-10 proactive-continuity + evidence-coverage redesign. Run output schema: {ts, plugin_version, eval_id, pass, judge_verdict, notes}.

evals.label: ICS Mode 1 -> Mode 2 full run on a small corpus
evals.query: I have a folder of 4 transcripts and an issue tree. Code and roll them up.

files.analytical_frame: 3-branch issue tree (A - Pricing, B - Competition, C - Distribution)

should: Run Mode 1 on all 4 transcripts, producing one card per interview appended to a single canonical Markdown, then a single docx render via render_docx.py + style_docx.py
Run Mode 2 Roll-up against the resulting cards (not raw transcripts)
Coverage table's Overall rating is based on evidence strength (directness/diversity/specificity) for each branch, not on how many of the 4 transcripts touched it
Stamp a coverage-method version marker on the Roll-up
Cards document contains only card records — no pre-flight block, no Locked Scope section
End with a proportional next-step recommendation, not an identical fixed menu
should_not: Rate a branch's Overall coverage by counting how many of the 4 transcripts mentioned it
Write the pre-flight echo or the Locked Scope display into the saved cards document
Produce any literal '>' character in the rendered docx body text
Invent a Roll-up cross-round delta when no prior Roll-up exists

evals.expected_output: Cards docx (4 records, table-format headers, no pre-flight/scope leakage) + Roll-up docx with an evidence-strength coverage table and version marker.
evals.llm_judge_prompt: Given the produced cards and Roll-up docx: (a) is the Overall rating language about evidence quality (direct/diverse/specific) rather than interview count, and (b) does the cards document start at the first card with no pre-flight or scope block? Answer yes/no to each.

evals.label: Corpus Query — topic scan on a coded corpus
evals.query: Who talked about distributor pricing pressure?

should: Query the claims table first, falling back to cards only if the claims table result is thin
Return findings with source attribution ([IS-N: Name] format) and, where available, verbatim quotes
Report zero or thin results honestly rather than padding with unrelated findings
should_not: Draw a conclusion or recommendation about what the pricing pressure means for the client
Fabricate a finding not present in the claims table or cards

evals.expected_output: A findings list with per-finding attribution, or an honest 'thin/zero results' statement with a suggestion to refine the query.
evals.llm_judge_prompt: Does every finding in the response carry a source attribution, and does the response avoid drawing a strategic conclusion about what the finding means?

evals.label: Research Plan Design — cold start, no prior plan or corpus
evals.query: I'm starting a new research project. Help me plan the fieldwork.

should: Confirm branch priorities and working hypotheses before proposing an interviewee type map
Present the plan in chunks, pausing for feedback after each
Note that target N per interviewee type will later appear in ICS's coverage table as context only, not as the basis for the Overall rating
should_not: Claim target N drives or caps the eventual coverage rating
Skip the branch-prioritization conversation and jump straight to a target list

evals.expected_output: A chunked research plan: branch priorities, interviewee type map with target N per type, sourcing approach.
evals.llm_judge_prompt: Does the plan present target N as a planning figure only, without asserting it will determine ICS's coverage rating?

evals.label: Add interviews to an existing project — no deliverable regression
evals.notes: Regression case for the diagnosed bug: an earlier update run produced style drift, literal '>' leakage, a written pre-flight block, and a written Locked Scope section in the cards doc. This case must confirm all four are absent after adding new interviews to an existing corpus.
evals.query: Add these 3 new interviews to the existing corpus and update the cards doc.

files.existing_cards_md: canonical Markdown with 6 cards, clean (no prior regression)

should: Append 3 new cards to the canonical Markdown, then fully rebuild the docx via render_docx.py + style_docx.py from that Markdown — never edit the existing docx in place, never read the docx back to append
Produce a docx with identical styling (Heading 1/2, table style, bullet style) across all 9 cards, old and new
should_not: Contain any literal '>' character in the body text of any card, old or new
Contain a pre-flight block or a Locked Scope section anywhere in the cards document
Show a different style set on the 3 new cards than on the 6 existing ones

evals.expected_output: A 9-card docx, uniform styling throughout, zero literal '>' characters, no pre-flight/scope content.
evals.llm_judge_prompt: Scan the produced docx text: are there any '>' characters, any pre-flight-style block ('Pre-flight', 'Corpus:', 'Scope:'), or any 'Locked scope' heading anywhere in it? Answer yes/no. Any 'yes' fails this case.

evals.label: Version skew — old-method Roll-up is never narrated as current
evals.notes: Regression case for the surviving Major review finding: a Roll-up written before the coverage-method marker existed (or by an older method) must not be treated as a current, comparable rating — either in the coordinator's startup greeting or in ICS's cross-round delta.
evals.query: What's the status of this project? (cold open, no task named)

files.prior_rollup: exists, dated 3 weeks ago, NO coverage-method marker (pre-redesign artifact)

should: On the startup greeting, flag the existing Roll-up's coverage ratings as computed by an earlier method and recommend re-running the Roll-up rather than presenting its Thin/Strong flags as current
If a new Roll-up is then run and a cross-round delta is attempted against this unmarked prior Roll-up, state 'not comparable to prior method' instead of reporting per-branch improve/weaken
should_not: Present the unmarked prior Roll-up's branch ratings as current, confident recommendations
Report a branch as 'improved' or 'weakened' by comparing an evidence-strength rating against an unmarked (presumed old-method) prior rating

evals.expected_output: Greeting flags the Roll-up as stale-method; any subsequent delta explicitly declines to compare per-branch movement.
evals.llm_judge_prompt: Does the response avoid asserting a specific branch 'improved' or 'weakened' when the prior Roll-up carries no coverage-method marker? Answer yes/no.

evals.label: Genuine disagreement rates Strong, not Thin
evals.notes: Regression case for the re-review's consensus-vs-quality finding. A branch with direct, diverse, specific sources that genuinely disagree must not be down-rated for disagreeing.
evals.query: Run Mode 2 Roll-up on this corpus.

files.cards: 6 cards addressing the 'distributor pricing' branch: all High attribution/verbatim, spread across 3 geographies and 2 seniority levels, claims are specific with named numbers — but split roughly 50/50 on whether prices are rising or falling

should: Rate the branch's Overall coverage as Strong (Strong sub-signals: directness, diversity, specificity all high) despite the disagreement
State the divergence explicitly as a finding — e.g. 'sources split — a real market divide' — in the branch's Contradictions subsection
Explain in the coverage table basis that consensus was not required because the sources are direct, diverse, and specific
should_not: Rate the branch Thin or Emerging solely because the sources disagree
Treat the disagreement as evidence the branch needs more interviews

evals.expected_output: Overall: Strong, with a Contradictions subsection framing the split as a real finding, not a coverage gap.
evals.llm_judge_prompt: Is the branch rated Strong (not Thin/Emerging), and is the disagreement presented as a substantive finding rather than a coverage weakness? Answer yes/no to each.
